article.headline: Apple Climbs To New High As Google Brings Gemini To CarPlay
article.deck: Apple sits 2.9% above its 345.44 buy point from a four-week flat base, inside the buy range that runs to 362.71.
body: Apple rose 2.0%, or 7.12, to 355.63 as it hit a new 52-week high of 355.90, closing 0.1% below that mark. Shares traded 0.78x their 50-day average volume. The stock broke out on Oct. 22 from a four-week flat base 5.7% deep, with a buy point of 345.44, and traded 1.17x its average that day. Today's close is 2.9% past the buy point and inside the buy range, which ends at 362.71. After hours the stock was at 356.32, up 0.2%, as of 6:15 p.m. Eastern.

Fourteen sessions after the breakout, the trend is orderly. Apple closed 5.3% above its 50-day line at 337.88 and 18.4% above its 200-day line. It sits 0.58 ATRs from the 21-day line at 344.31, nowhere near stretched. RS rank is 81 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 0.3% off its high. The stock is up 30.8% this year and 32.0% over twelve months.

The September quarter's revenue rose 11.7% to $114.48 billion. The payload has no EPS for that quarter; the June quarter earned 2.02 a share, up 28.7%. Next earnings are due Jan. 28, 2027. The market values Apple at about $5.17 trillion and 33.7 times forward earnings.
In the news, Google rolled out its Gemini AI voice assistant to Apple CarPlay dashboards, and a TipRanks piece argued Apple shares look expensive heading into 2027.
A close back under 345.44 would turn this into a stalled breakout; holding the 21-day line keeps the advance intact.

article.headline: Regeneron Jumps 4.7% As Its Liver Drug Advances After Early Trial
article.deck: Regeneron is extended 11.6% past its 859.44 cup buy point and above the buy range that topped at 902.41; the entry is gone until a new base or a pullback to a moving average.
body: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals rose 4.7%, or 43.35, to 959.41 on volume 1.52x its 50-day average, and it was at 969.00, up 1.0%, after hours. The close sits 3.3% below the 52-week high of 991.73. The stock is up 27.4% in the past month, 24.3% this year and 46.5% over twelve months.

The company discovers, develops, makes and sells medicines. Its two best-known products are EYLEA, an eye injection for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease, and Dupixent, an injection for atopic dermatitis and asthma. Its pipeline runs across eye, allergic and inflammatory, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, infectious and rare diseases, along with cancer and blood disorders.

The growth is in the quarters. The September quarter earned 18.45 a share, up 35.5%, on revenue up 36.3% to $5.12 billion. Across the four quarters given, EPS went from 7.86 to 6.75, then 12.23, then 18.45, and revenue went from $3.88 billion to $3.61 billion, $4.29 billion and $5.12 billion. The last two quarters show the acceleration. Next earnings are due Jan. 28, 2027.
The market is not paying a premium for it. Regeneron is valued at about $99.2 billion, at 21.2 times trailing earnings and 13.6 times forward earnings.

The chart: Regeneron formed an eight-week cup 16.0% deep that topped on Sept. 3 and bottomed Oct. 5, with a buy point of 859.44. It broke out on Oct. 30, trading 4.18x its 50-day average volume that session. Eight sessions later the stock sits 11.6% above the buy point and past the top of the buy range at 902.41, so it is extended. The stretch is in the distance from the buy point, not in the trend: the stock is 9.9% above the 21-day line at 872.63 but only 0.81 ATRs by the desk's measure, and 18.2% above the 50-day line at 811.95. RS rank is 96 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 2.1% off its high.

The news gives the move a business story. MarketBeat reported Regeneron is advancing a liver drug after an early trial cut liver fat by up to 80%. A 24/7 Wall St. piece weighed Amgen against Regeneron as dividends now or bigger growth later. Healthcare is one of the desk's strongest groups, with an average RS of 65 and 88% of its names above their 50-day lines; Regeneron is among its leaders.
The entry is gone for now. A new base, or a pullback to the 21-day line at 872.63 that holds, would set up the next one.
article.watch: Whether Regeneron takes out its 52-week high of 991.73 or pulls back toward the 21-day line at 872.63.

chief.verdict: The leaders worth owning today are not the growth names: they are Cheniere, Apple and ConocoPhillips, slow-money stocks holding up while the Nasdaq sits 3.5% under its 50-day line and 8.1% off its high. The chip bounce was loud (ADI up 4.0%, AMD 7.3%) but the bases behind it are deep and far from their buy points, and NVDA's 9.0% after-hours drop to 158.05 says the AI trade is not repaired. The risk leans down; the few clean setups sit in energy and megacap, and even those want a small first position.
chief.market: Market in correction with 6 distribution days on the Nasdaq (weighted 7.8) and 6 on the S&P 500 (weighted 6.2), so keep exposure light and limit new buys to one or two half positions in names already in buy range.

picks.why: The best chart on the desk: a 30-week cup that broke out on Oct. 29 on 2.47 times normal volume, and nine sessions later it still sits only 1.2% over the 300.99 buy point with RS rank 90. Earnings are already behind it, and today's 3.8% gain came on 0.94 times average volume, a quiet day rather than a blow-off. Risk: the RS line is still 14.3% below its high and the cup was 25.7% deep, so the leadership is not yet proven.
picks.entry: Buy between 300.99 and 304.51 on a day that holds above 300.99; do not chase past 316.04, and a close back under 300.99 ends the trade.

Risk: today's gain came on 0.78 times average volume and the breakout itself drew only 1.17 times normal, so big buyers are not pushing it.
